content: # Chef Jobs Abroad: How to Work in Europe and the Middle East from Bangladesh The culinary world knows no borders. For talented and certified Bangladeshi chefs, the globe is their kitchen. In 2026, the demand for **chef jobs abroad for Bangladeshi** professionals is at an all-time high, driven by growth in international tourism and shortages of skilled culinary staff globally. This guide provides a strategic, legally compliant roadmap to transition from a local student to an international culinary professional. --- ## Quick Navigation: Jump to Regions - [Middle East Opportunities & Requirements](#middle-east-jobs) - [Europe & German Opportunity Card Pathways](#europe-jobs) - [Maldives & Luxury Resort Placements](#maldives-jobs) --- ## Official Regulatory Authorities & Visa Compliance When migrating from Bangladesh for skilled employment, you must comply with the guidelines set by: 1. **Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment**: Overseeing skilled migration. 2. **Bureau of Manpower, Employment and Training (BMET)**: Issuing the mandatory Smart Card and registration for overseas employment. 3. **German Skilled Immigration Act (Fachkräfteeinwanderungsgesetz)**: Providing streamlined visa processes for vocational certificate holders. --- ## 1. Middle East Placements (UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar) The Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) region is the largest employer of Bangladeshi culinary talent. Luxury hotels and restaurants in Dubai, Riyadh, and Doha actively recruit skilled cooks. - **Visa Type**: Employment Visa sponsored by the employer. - **Requirements**: Certified proof of culinary training (NSDA Level-2/3), medical fitness clearance (GAMCA), and a successfully cleared practical 'Trade Test'. - **BMET Clearance**: Mandatory BMET registration and Smart Card verification before boarding. ## 2. Europe & German Skilled Immigration Pathways Under the updated **German Skilled Immigration Act (2024-2026)**, skilled chefs with recognized vocational training can apply for employment or job-seeker visas (Opportunity Card / Chancenkarte) directly. - **Visa Type**: German Skilled Worker Visa / Opportunity Card. - **Requirements**: A recognized culinary diploma (such as CIB's 6-Month Diploma), basic German language skills (A2/B1 level), or professional English. You must have your credentials verified by the German Central Office for Foreign Education (ZAB). - **Salary Potential**: European placements offer high-income packages starting from EUR 2,500 to EUR 4,500 monthly, along with pathways to permanent residency. ## 3. Maldives & Luxury Resort Placements Maldives' high-end tourism industry operates hundreds of luxury private island resorts, which prioritize chefs with international training. - **Visa Type**: Maldives Work Permit sponsored by the resort. - **Requirements**: Hands-on culinary training, experience in global cuisines (French, Mediterranean, Japanese), and strict adherence to **ISO-HACCP** safety standards. At [The Culinary Institute of Bangladesh (CIB)](/en/about), our curriculum is specifically mapped to these international kitchen standards. Under the guidance of principal **Dewan Ismail** and veteran mentors, CIB graduates receive training that makes passing foreign trade tests and securing visas straightforward. --- ## Step-by-Step Visa & Migration Process for Bangladeshi Chefs To move abroad legally as a skilled chef, you must follow the official government channel: 1. **Step 1: Get Certified**: Complete an NSDA-accredited, BTEB-approved course at CIB and obtain your certificate. 2. **Step 2: Attestation**: Get your culinary certificates and transcript attested by the Ministry of Education and Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MoFA) in Dhaka. 3. **Step 3: ZAB Evaluation (For Europe)**: Submit your documents to ZAB (Zentralstelle für ausländisches Bildungswesen) in Germany to verify equivalence to German standards. 4. **Step 4: GAMCA Medical Test (For Gulf countries)**: Undergo the mandatory medical checkup at a GAMCA-approved center. 5. **Step 5: Obtain BMET Smart Card**: Register on the **Ami Probashi** portal, attend the mandatory pre-departure briefing (PDO), and obtain your BMET Smart Card. --- ## Summary of High-Demand Regions for Chefs | Region / Country | Average Entry Salary (Monthly) | Visa Complexity | IELTS / Language Required | Key Skill Demand | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **UAE (Dubai/Abu Dhabi)** | USD 800 - 1,500 | Low | No | Continental & Arabic Cuisines | | **Saudi Arabia (Riyadh)** | USD 900 - 1,800 | Low | No | Banquet & Mass Food Production | | **Maldives (Resorts)** | USD 1,000 - 2,000 | Medium | Basic English | HACCP Compliance, Pastry, Fine Dining | | **Germany** | EUR 2,200 - 3,500 | High | German A2/B1 | Pastry, Bakeries, International Cuisine | | **Australia** | AUD 3,500 - 5,000 | High | General IELTS (5.0+) | Commercial Cookery, Kitchen Supervision | --- ## Launch Your Global Career with CIB Preparing for a culinary job abroad requires more than just cooking; it requires a strategic video portfolio, interview preparation, and understanding international food safety standards. CIB provides [conditional placement support](/en/admission) and connects our alumni with reputable global recruiters. To learn more about our campus facilities, visit our [About CIB](/en/about) page, or view our mentors on the [Expert Culinary Mentors](/en/expert-culinary-mentors) page. Apply for our upcoming batch and take your first step toward a prestigious global career today.
